criteria.name: Register match
criteria.reason: The tone is appropriate for low-stakes interface copy. The imperative verb 'Get' is direct and action-focused, matching the style of approved low-stakes examples like LEM-011 and LEM-012.

criteria.name: Humour boundary
criteria.reason: No humour is present. The copy is straightforward and functional, appropriate for a button label at low stakes.

criteria.name: Plain language calibration
criteria.reason: The phrase 'Get my price' uses simple, direct language without unnecessary jargon or untranslated insurance terminology. It names the concrete action the reader can control.

criteria.name: Direct address
criteria.reason: No named subject or addressee is provided by the interface for this button label; there's no pet, home or person name to reference, so direct-address cannot be evaluated.

criteria.name: Character budget
criteria.reason: No declared interface character limit was provided for this string, so fit cannot be assessed.

criteria.name: Action verb consistency
criteria.reason: Approved low-stakes button labels use all caps with concrete verbs (e.g. 'GET DISCOUNTS', 'FINALIZE PAYMENT'). This draft uses sentence case ('Get my price') instead of the required all-caps button convention, so it doesn't match the surrounding product flow's established mechanics for interface actions.

compliance.reason: The draft consists solely of the button label 'Get my price.' It contains no guarantee of an outcome, no removed disclaimer, no unsupported judgement claim about how Lemonade evaluates a customer, no contradiction of known policy, and no attributed quote or factual public claim requiring a source. Per instructions, an isolated navigation/button label is not failed for missing surrounding context. The label also names a concrete action rather than using a generic 'click here' phrasing, so it passes the compliance check.
